findings.highlight: There is nothing moving, and every living thing is asleep.
findings.evidenceJa: 沈殿した闇
findings.governingReading: The active narration moves from midnight to settled darkness and the town-as-deep-sea image.
findings.explanation: The non-Realta branch restores an inactive assertion that every living thing sleeps.

findings.highlight: a dark sea that only has moonlight to illuminate it
findings.evidenceJa: 月の明かりだけを寄る辺にした、暗い深海
findings.governingReading: The town resembles a dark deep sea whose only point of support or refuge is the glimpsed moonlight.
findings.explanation: The English drops the depth and replaces the relational 寄る辺 image with simple illumination.

findings.highlight: There is some wind.
findings.evidenceJa: 風が出るな
findings.governingReading: Saber quietly predicts or observes that the wind is beginning to rise.
findings.explanation: “Some wind” changes the onset into a vague quantity and conflicts with the windless ground explicitly described.

findings.highlight: Looking up at the wind in the sky
findings.evidenceJa: わずかに耳朶を震わせる上空の風
findings.governingReading: She looks toward the high wind that faintly trembles her earlobe.
findings.explanation: The English omits the precise bodily sensation through which the apparently inaudible wind reaches her.

findings.highlight: proves their existence to this day
findings.evidenceJa: 現代においてなお、彼女の在り方を決定づける
findings.governingReading: Even in the present age, her undefeated armored figure defines her mode of being.
findings.explanation: The English turns characterization into proof that an ambiguously plural entity exists.

findings.highlight: A knight among knights, true to decorum, and acting on its master’s order.
findings.evidenceJa: 主の意思を代行する騎士の中の騎士
findings.governingReading: Saber is a knight among knights who observes decorum and acts in place of her lord’s will.
findings.explanation: The English calls her “it,” destabilizes gender and address, and reduces representing the Master’s will to acting on an order.

findings.highlight: But that ends today.
findings.evidenceJa: それも今宵で終わった
findings.governingReading: That ideal of never defying her lord ends tonight.
findings.explanation: “Today” loses the nocturnal immediacy of the interlude.

findings.highlight: will not be able to fix his personality
findings.evidenceJa: その甘さを捨てきれないだろう
findings.governingReading: Saber believes this Master cannot discard his gentleness or softness.
findings.explanation: The English recasts a morally charged trait he cannot relinquish as a defective personality to be fixed.

findings.highlight: She has no more interest in the shed her master is sleeping in.
findings.evidenceJa: もはや主の眠る土蔵に関心はない
findings.governingReading: Once armed, Saber no longer directs her attention toward the shed where her Master sleeps.
findings.explanation: “No more interest” suggests emotional indifference rather than disciplined redirection toward battle.

findings.highlight: the will to defeat her enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵を屠る意思だけ
findings.governingReading: Armed, Saber contains only the will to slaughter the enemy.
findings.explanation: “Defeat” softens the lethal severity of her chosen role.

findings.highlight: The Ryuudou Temple located on top of it.
findings.evidenceJa: その中腹に位置する柳洞寺
findings.governingReading: Ryuudou Temple lies partway up the sacred mountain.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the temple from the mountainside to the summit.

findings.highlight: is already contaminated
findings.evidenceJa: とうの昔に汚されている
findings.governingReading: The land’s lifeline was polluted long ago.
findings.explanation: “Already” fails to convey that the corruption dates far back, weakening Saber’s contrast with memory.

findings.highlight: She runs through the scene.
findings.evidenceJa: 駆け抜ける景色
findings.governingReading: The scenery streams past as Saber runs.
findings.explanation: The English makes “scene” a space she traverses and loses the moving visual perspective.

findings.highlight: Saber feels so complete that she can break through any obstacles.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーとしての自信だった
findings.governingReading: Her resolve to break through even Berserker is confidence in herself as Saber.
findings.explanation: The non-Realta branch restores an inactive assertion of personal completeness and universalizes the obstacles.

findings.highlight: Even for she who has seen many heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 多くの英霊を見てきた彼女とて
findings.governingReading: Even she, who has seen many Heroic Spirits, has never encountered a Servant dressed this way.
findings.explanation: The English uses a subject pronoun after a preposition.

findings.highlight: has no fearful aspects nor a fearful weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 恐れるべき箇所も、驚異を感じるほどの武装もない
findings.governingReading: The man displays neither an obvious point to fear nor armament imposing enough to feel threatening.
findings.explanation: “Fearful aspects” and “fearful weapon” are malformed and blur the distinction between readable weakness and equipment pressure.

findings.highlight: a way to seize a certain kill
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を必殺する手段
findings.governingReading: Saber’s instinct warns that this Servant possesses a means certain to kill her.
findings.explanation: The English phrase is nonidiomatic and obscures who faces certain death.

findings.highlight: but above it, Saber’s location is at a disadvantage
findings.evidenceJa: それ以上にセイバーの位置はあまりに不利だ
findings.governingReading: More than the sword’s unreadable reach, Saber’s lower position is severely unfavorable.
findings.explanation: “Above it” mistranslates comparative priority and further confuses an already spatial tactical explanation.

findings.highlight: Which Servant are you?
findings.evidenceJa: その身は如何なるサーヴァントか
findings.governingReading: Saber asks what kind or class of Servant he is.
findings.explanation: The English asks which individual Servant he is, missing the class information she explicitly seeks.

findings.highlight: I would not expect for you to make a face like that.
findings.evidenceJa: そのような顔をされるとは心外であった
findings.governingReading: Assassin says her reaction is unexpected and regrettable after his courteous introduction.
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical “expect for” construction.

findings.highlight: to have no match in this large world
findings.evidenceJa: 慶長の世に並ぶ者なし
findings.governingReading: He was reputed to be without peer in the Keichō era.
findings.explanation: The English mistakes a named historical era for the size of the world.

findings.highlight: There was only one who knew the existence of this swordsman. That being the worthy rival of the rare-skilled swordsman
findings.evidenceJa: 希代の剣豪の好敵手として祭り上げられた剣士を知る者など、この世でおそらくただ一人
findings.governingReading: The legendary Sasaki was elevated through oral tradition as the worthy rival of an extraordinary swordsman; perhaps only the unrecorded foe who defeated him truly knew him.
findings.explanation: The English tangles subject and rival, making the “one who knew” into the worthy rival and leaving the historical relation incoherent.

findings.highlight: a swordsman who is usually not treated as a hero
findings.evidenceJa: 本来ならば英霊として扱われぬ剣士
findings.governingReading: This swordsman would ordinarily not qualify to be treated as a Heroic Spirit.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a supernatural classification boundary with ordinary heroic reputation.

findings.highlight: You have me.
findings.evidenceJa: まいりました
findings.governingReading: Saber concedes that Assassin’s courtesy has put her in a difficult position requiring reciprocal introduction.
findings.explanation: The English can read as surrender or capture during a duel that has not begun.

findings.highlight: these swords shall be enough to know our enemies
findings.evidenceJa: 敵を知るにはこの刀だけで十分
findings.governingReading: Assassin says this one blade is enough for the two warriors to know an enemy.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the weapon and obscures his claim that combat through his blade replaces verbal identity.

findings.highlight: readies her sword close to her
findings.evidenceJa: 深く剣を構え直す
findings.governingReading: Saber resets into a deep, committed guard.
findings.explanation: “Close to her” changes depth of stance into distance between sword and body.
